rows: 22 places · the signature of Holland Village

rows.w: A MICHELIN Bib Gourmand hawker across two adjoining stalls: noodle soup or 'dry' noodles with minced pork, pork balls or fish balls hand-made on the spot — the yellowtail fishballs are the draw.

Fried to order over a superheated wok so the flat rice noodles take on real wok hei before the gravy goes in — the brown-sauce beef hor fun is the bestseller; written up by Dr Leslie Tay and Miss Tam Chiak and tested by Seth Lui as one of Singapore's best-rated hor fun.

rows.n: Yuan Hokkien Fried Prawn Mee (Ghim Moh)
rows.w: A Margaret Drive Food Centre transplant: white and yellow noodles wok-fried down in a rich stock of prawn heads, squid and pork bones — one of the Ghim Moh picks shared by Women's Weekly and Her World.

The kway chap stall Miss Tam Chiak calls chef Daniel Tay's favourite: silky rice sheets in a herbal braising broth with a spread of braised pork, offal and egg — written up by Daniel Food Diary, SG Food on Foot and in Eatbook's 13 best Holland Drive stalls.

rows.n: Lao Chen Ji Sarawak Kolo Mee (Holland Drive)
rows.w: Springy Sarawak kolo mee, served with yong tau foo pieces — a regulars' favourite named by HungryGoWhere, Daniel Food Diary (2023), Johor Kaki and Women's Weekly.

The most popular carrot cake at Ghim Moh — a family stall that makes both the radish cake and the chye poh from scratch daily; the queue starts at 6:30am and limited portions sell out, rewarding early birds with strong wok hei.

rows.n: Fifty Year Yong Tau Foo (Holland Drive)
rows.w: Freshly made Hakka yong tau foo over flat mee kia noodles — a fifty-year name that HungryGoWhere, Johor Kaki and Eatbook all list among Holland Drive's regulars' picks.

rows.n: Margaret Drive Sin Kee Chicken Rice
rows.w: Steamed chicken rice since 1978; on the Michelin Bib Gourmand list since 2018.

rows.n: Yuan Authentic Thai Stewed Beef Noodle (Ghim Moh)
rows.w: Run by a cook from Chiang Rai: Thai stewed and sliced beef noodle soup — beefy, aromatic broth, beef balls, slices and tendon, small bowls from under $3 — a Thai hawker kitchen in an otherwise Chinese-heavy centre (Eatbook review; Women's Weekly and Her World Ghim Moh lists).

A short-hours roast-meat counter (10am-2pm, Thursday to Sunday) for roast duck, crackling roast pork and char siew — reviewed by Miss Tam Chiak and listed by Women's Weekly / Her World among Ghim Moh's best.

rows.n: Yap Kee Wanton Egg Noodles (Holland Drive)
rows.w: Wanton mee made with egg noodles supplied by the owner's brother in Johor Bahru (Johor Kaki) — on HungryGoWhere's and Eatbook's Holland Drive lists.
One of Holland Drive's busier stalls: springy Hakka noodles heaped with yong tau foo pieces and crisp fried wantons — a generous neighbourhood bowl.

rows: 5 places · the top tier, graded within each area

rows.w: The Holland-Ghim Moh district's great hawker centre: opened in 1978, rebuilt in a 2015 facelift and refreshed again in a March-May 2024 renovation, yet still old-school neighbourhood in feel — around 72 cooked-food stalls over a wet market, famous for chwee kueh, braised duck, hor fun and carrot cake, a short walk from Buona Vista MRT.

A household name since 1959 and a Michelin Guide pick: soft-but-springy steamed rice cakes (minimum four) heaped with chye poh fried over a charcoal stove, which gives the preserved radish a smokier depth than the gas-cooked norm.

Holland Drive's headline stall and a Michelin Bib Gourmand year after year (incl. 2024 and 2025): every claypot is cooked from scratch over charcoal, so the grains stay separate with a crackling crust — call ahead, because the wait can run to an hour.

Ghim Moh's Michelin Bib Gourmand duck stall: boneless Teochew-style braised duck over rice, kway teow or congee, dressed in a dark herbal gravy whose braising stock is reused and replenished daily — a $3-$5 bowl with years of depth in it.

rows: 1 place · kept for the record, newest check first

rows.n: Guan Kee Fried Kway Teow — CLOSED
rows.w: Started in 1969 and at Ghim Moh since 1978, this was one of Singapore's most-queued char kway teow stalls (Bib Gourmand 2019) — it closed for good on 28 Nov 2023 when its 77-year-old owner retired after fainting at the wok. Kept here as a flagged closure.
